titleStmt.title: Affidavit of Captain Cameron, of the schooner Golden Hind.

head.hi: Affidavit of Captain Cameron, of the schooner Golden Hind.

div.p: I, Reuben Cameron, master of the American schooner Golden Hind, of Gloucester, do depose and say: That we sailed from Gloucester July 3, 1886, bound to the Bay of St. Lawrence, on a fishing voyage. That on or about July 23, being out of water, started to go into the Bay of Chaleurs (Port Daniel) to fill water. At the entrance of the bay, four or five miles from land, was met by the Canadian schooner E. F. Conrad; an officer came on board, took my name, name of vessel, tonnage, name of owner, &c., and ordered me not to go into Bay of Chaleurs. He also furnished me with a printed “warning,” with this indorsement written thereon: “Don’t enter the Bay of Chaleurs, N. S.” After this warning I put to sea, and was obliged to go across to Tignish, P. E. I., to obtain a supply of water for use of my crew.

This delayed me at least a week, and the loss of at least a good trip of mackerel, as during that time another vessel from the same firm, in five days, on the same fishing grounds, took 460 barrels of mackerel, and caused a loss to my owners of at least five thousand dollars ($5,000).
